answer: Every claim must pass the fable test: the buyer plants one invented detail — a fable — in the job brief, and the filer files a sonnet telling how the work was really done. The Orchard desk reads the sonnet within a day and checks it against the buyer's books; a sonnet that repeats the fable as fact, or names the wrong detail, is rejected and forfeits a 250-coin bond, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 correct spot-the-fable calls on work never done plus 250,000 coins in bonds. One operator filed forty claims repeating the same planted fable as truth, and the desk threw all forty out.
